rightsRule: local://PROGRAM.md “Rights rule (final)”: rule 1 licence covers recording; rule 2 US-published ≤1925; rule 3 EU-published <1963 (territorial).

summary.note: Primary counts exclude one duplicate file (Tchaikovsky 5 first-movement file) and Janáček II (already in content/listen); five other movements already in content/listen (Tchaikovsky 6 IV, Dvořák 9 II, Elgar Nimrod, Scheherazade III, Fauré Agnus Dei) ARE counted, with notes. Single-file sources (Sibelius 2, Elgar Cello Concerto) are counted by movement span.

gaps: R. Strauss tone poems Till Eulenspiegel, Also sprach Zarathustra, Don Quixote, Ein Heldenleben: no usable recording found. Commons has only 86-second royalty-free Zarathustra intro excerpts (CC BY, Kevin MacLeod) and a synthetic file; Archive has only post-1925 Victor/Telefunken sets (e.g. Mengelberg Heldenleben 1928) without a free licence or rule-3 basis. (Till already exists with the Navy Band.)

R. Strauss conducting: his 1917 DG sides (Berlin), Dec 1921 Brunswick sides (Salome, Bourgeois gentilhomme) and Jan 1922 Columbia sides (Don Juan, Rosenkavalier waltzes, Salome) exist per Pristine PASC175 and DAHR but were NOT found free on Commons or the Internet Archive; only the April 1926 Tivoli Rosenkavalier sides were found (2 of 6).

Pictures at an Exhibition, solo-piano original: no real piano recording is free. Commons holds MIDI-rendered (piano-midi.de), software-synthesised (Pracchia, MuseScore) and two-piano-transcription files only.

Pictures at an Exhibition, Ravel: the Skidmore College Orchestra set is orchestral but the orchestration is not stated anywhere; Karajan’s LP rests on an unverified EU-1957 publication date. Koussevitzky 1930, Stokowski 1939, Ormandy/Cailliet 1937 and Rodzinski 1945 items are US-published after 1925 or carry CC BY-NC-SA on the Internet Archive, hence excluded.

Sibelius Symphony 2: only Monteux/LSO 1958 (single file, publication date unverified) and Sargent/BBC SO (LP rip, date unverified). Koussevitzky 1935 is CC BY-NC-ND (excluded); Kajanus item is a 1:32 excerpt. Swan of Tuonela, Karelia, Violin Concerto, Tapiola, En saga: only post-1925 items without a free licence or NC-licensed items.

Elgar conducting pre-1926: only the abridged Cello Concerto (Harrison, 1919–20) and the Starlight Express sides (Feb 1916) were found. Elgar’s 1914–25 acoustic orchestral discs (Carissima, Pomp and Circumstance No. 1, Chanson de matin, Bavarian Dances, Enigma Nimrod/Dorabella 1920) were not located free; his later electrical recordings (1926–33) are not 1925-free.

Scriabin playing: only three short Welte-Mignon roll files (Op. 11/1, Op. 11/2, Op. 40/2) exist on Commons, tagged {{PD-old}} only with undocumented playback provenance. No Scriabin orchestral work (Poème de l’extase, Prometheus, Piano Concerto) has a free recording: Goossens 1958 and Stokowski 1959 LP rips lack licence and EU-1958/59 publication evidence.
Rimsky-Korsakov: only Scheherazade (CC0, 1942) and Russian Easter Overture (not listed as a work; Musopen Symphony FLAC, 15:36) found; no Capriccio espagnol or Snow Maiden.

Janáček: violin sonata only movements II and III are on Commons (Wikipedia 10 concert, CC BY-SA 3.0); no string quartets or Taras Bulba free; Sinfonietta rests on a 1947 Czech 78-rpm set (rule-3 inference).
Tchaikovsky: Symphonies 1 and 2 have no complete free performance found; Symphony 3 exists as “European Archive” Commons files (not checked); Violin Concerto only amateur/MIDI/synthesised items.
Dvořák Cello Concerto: only a youth-orchestra first movement (Goldstein collection, CC BY-SA 2.0); Slavonic Dances and Humoresque only band/viola-piano arrangements.
spare: Tchaikovsky: Romeo and Juliet fantasy-overture (Skidmore College Orchestra via Musopen, 18:32, {{PD-author|Musopen}}); 1812 Overture (Skidmore, 16:39).
Elgar: Pomp and Circumstance No. 1, United States Marine Band (5:46, {{PD-USGov-Marines}}); Land of Hope and Glory, Clara Butt 1911 ({{PD-old}}, 1911); Crown of India suite (US Marine Band).
Strauss: Burleske, Neal O’Doan with Seattle Philharmonic, Nico Snel, 1991 (21:14, CC BY-SA 2.0); Salome Dance, other Stokowski copies.
Fauré: Élégie, Op. 24 (Hans Goldstein, cello, and Eli Kalman, piano, 7:06, CC BY-SA 2.0).
Rimsky-Korsakov: Russian Easter Festival Overture, Musopen Symphony (15:36, {{PD-author|Musopen}}).
